text:
The Avalanche found out on Saturday that Nathan MacKinnon will miss about a month and Cale Makar about two weeks, both hurt against Ottawa earlier in the week, as The Athletic's Julian McKenzie reported. Then they went out at the Bell Centre and beat the Canadiens 4-1. The Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal called it "Colorado's best win to date", and it's hard to argue with him.

Colorado struck first and early. Fedor Svechkov scored 3:57 in, and Brock Nelson made it 2-0 late in the first on a shot that goes in about 5% of the time. Nick Suzuki got Montreal back in it midway through the second with a spinning backhand, a 4% chance that was the least likely goal of the night. Artturi Lehkonen restored the two-goal lead on a power play 4:14 into the third, pushing Colorado's win chance to 92%, and Nicolas Roy finished it late.

Mackenzie Blackwood was the difference when it was close: 25 saves on 26 shots, 1.4 goals better than those shots usually allow, and the player who added most to the win by our measure. His best stop came on Cole Caufield in the second, with Colorado up 2-0. Jakub Dobes was solid at the other end, stopping Nazem Kadri's 24% look in the third, and Kadri's four shots added up to 1.44 expected goals on his own, more than anyone in the game.

The underlying game was close for two periods, then Colorado took over the third, and the Avs won it in 65% of our replays. Lehkonen is now on the top line and the top units on both special teams, per Rawal. That's the new reality, as the Denver Post's Corey Masisak put it, for the next few weeks: the Avalanche go home from a successful road trip as a different team. Montreal, with Suzuki reportedly playing through an injury, will want this one back.
headline: No MacKinnon, no Makar, and the Avs win in Montreal anyway
